newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes firmer, follows U.S. heating oil.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes firmer, follows U.S. heating oil.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended firmer on Wednesday in the wake of stronger NYMEX heating oil futures and amid a perception of good technical support, traders said.
March Brent futures closed 51 cents a barrel firmer at $22.76. February IPE gas oil closed earlier $4.00 a tonne up at $204.50.
"Everything is following U.S. heating oil," one IPE dealer said.
NYMEX February heating oil was 2.17 cents a gallon firmer at 2028 GMT, trading at 69.00 cents.
Traders said that the contract's strength was a result of colder weather forecasts, combined with bullish inventory data.

Independent forecasters Weather Services Corp. said heating oil demand would be higher than average in the key markets in the U.S. northeast, while temperatures in Europe will also be colder towards the weekend.

And latest data from the Energy Information Administration (EIA) showed distillate stocks in the U.S. had fallen by 2.5 million barrels in the week to January 24, backing up earlier figures from the American Petroleum Institute.
This distillate draw was more than traders had been expecting.
While crude oil inventories rose over the week in question, they remain a huge 17.7 million barrels lower than at this time last year.

Traders said technical support for March Brent, which has held fast above the four-month low of $22.00, appeared to be solidifying. They pegged next resistance for this contract at $22.90 and then $23.00.
Traders said signs of increasing instability in Iraq were adding another layer of support.
White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said on Wednesday there were "a great deal of complicated internal struggles for power" going on inside Iraq.
A senior military officer also told journalists the wife of President Saddam Hussein had been placed under house arrest, and that Saddam was moving around more regularly to ensure his own safety.
But traders said the impact of this news was, at best, modest.
Brent intermonth spreads were little changed. The backwardation between March and April narrowed by five cents.
